comment: Every assertion in the test suite about how the REAL corpus ranks: the query, the lesson search.js must rank first (its topic-index id, which search.js --json reports and the eval split uses; NOT lesson_number, which differs for L1-L50), and (optionally) the keyword_map key that must name exactly that lesson. corpus-ranking.test.js runs every case and guards that no case names a holdout lesson. The retrieval eval's split tooling (evals/retrieval/lib.js applyHardTestRule) reads this file: a random lesson split is drawn, then every lesson a case here depends on is moved to dev. Add a real-corpus ranking assertion here, never inline in a test file. A case with "fused": true is asserted under search.js --fused (the RRF order) rather than the default keyword-first order.
